sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Arnhem is among the cities where street parking is already dear and set to become dearer. The council adopted the Parkeerverordening 2026 on 12 November 2025, with the levy applying from 1 January 2026: 4.60 euros an hour for street parking in the centre and several inner districts, 3.10 euros elsewhere, 149 euros a year for a resident permit and 552 euros for an unlimited business permit [5]. Street parking is paid Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 23:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 23:00 [13]. In June 2026 the new coalition agreement was reported to plan parking becoming 30 cents an hour more expensive on top of inflation, with no payment on Sunday mornings in some areas [10], and in September 2026 the city's financial plans were reported to have parking costs rising 2.1 percent a year plus 90 cents per parked hour in total, so that street parking in and around the centre would head towards 6 euros an hour; this is a plan, not a tariff in force [11].

The municipality's proposal for Parkeerbeleid 2025 of 30 September 2025 stated a wish to gradually scale back street parking in the centre, to study an underground garage inside the centrumring and to make the first resident permit outside the centre free; the council's vote is not shown in the document [4]. New housing rules adopted on 17 March 2026 add an A+ area covering the inner city and the station area where new homes can be exempt from building car parking provided alternatives, mainly bicycle parking, are realised [7]. Since 1 June 2026 central Arnhem has an environmental zone for diesel cars and buses and a zero-emission zone for vans and trucks [9]. A parking scan car has been used since April 2022 and issued almost 53,000 assessments in 2025, about 20 percent of which were objected to, according to the municipality's spokesperson as reported [6].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The development has been in how existing garages are used. A municipal proposal of December 2021 asked for 3.22 million euros for a first phase of refurbishing the Rozet garage, with a new entrance, about 60 extra spaces, a solar roof and at least 14 charging points; the council's decision is not shown in the document [2]. The same month a note proposed a 510,000-euro refurbishment pilot for the Musis garage [1]. Opposite Rozet, the Bartok Park Zuid housing is to have a guarded public bicycle store for about 650 bicycles, with construction expected to start in January 2027 [3]. The Musis garage now has a charging plaza with 40 points and Centraal has 14, while Rozet has none [15].

Park and ride is free: P+R GelreDome and P+R Station Arnhem Zuid are open 24 hours with only the public transport fare payable, though GelreDome is not available during major events [14]. For concerts at GelreDome in May 2026 parking required a pre-bought ticket and shuttle buses ran from Arnhem Centraal for 5.90 euros return [8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The three municipal garages, Centraal, Musis and Rozet, with 2,190 spaces, charge 0.70 euro per 10 minutes from 06:00 to 18:00, 1.70 euros an hour at night and 24 euros a day; Musis and Rozet subscriptions cost 2,297 euros a year and Centraal issues none [12]. Q-Park runs the Broerenstraat garage with 426 spaces [16], and the private Velperplein garage charges 1.00 euro per 20 minutes and 20 euros per 24 hours [17]. In 2019 the municipality counted the three garages full at the same time on a Saturday afternoon, with 72 percent of street spaces occupied [0], and a 2021 note found the municipal garages full on Saturday afternoon in both survey years during Covid [1].

Our data cover four garages with 2,319 spaces from the national parking feed: Centraal (1,050), Musis (690), Rozet (450) and Velperplein (129), measured for 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 57% on weekdays and 58% at weekends, weighted by spaces, so the garages are used as much on weekends as on working days. Rozet is the fullest at 64% on weekdays and 69% at weekends, Centraal and Musis are at 58% and 57%, and Velperplein is the quietest at 27%. All of the municipal garages reached full in single readings, in line with the earlier survey findings. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
